quote: Last year, we bought so last year, we got another electric car and we put in a hot tub, which is part of the reason we need more panels.
stewart_read: Customer volunteers two major load-increase signals (second EV, hot tub) unprompted — a strong forward-pulling hook for system-size justification. Rep logs it but does not reflect it back as a reason the appointment matters.
alternative_hypothesis: Rep may have judged this unnecessary since the customer is already sold and booking regardless, making the flip low-value on an already-warm orphaned lead.
coaching_implication: Coach the rep to briefly mirror high-value signals like this back to the customer ('so between the car and the hot tub, that's exactly the kind of usage growth the specialist will want to size for') — costs nothing and reinforces the appointment's purpose even on warm leads.

quote: house was 207, and the cars were $5.81.
stewart_read: Customer gives precise annual electricity spend broken out by house vs. vehicles — a rich, specific bill anchor. Rep acknowledges with 'Okay. Perfect.' and moves on without flipping it into emotional leverage.
alternative_hypothesis: The customer explicitly states this isn't a cost-payback conversation ('we're not looking at this from, like, a cost payback type situation'), so a bill-flip may be tonally mismatched to what the customer is asking for.
coaching_implication: Even when the customer frames the ask as non-financial, the rep can still log the number as useful sizing context for the closer rather than letting it pass with only an acknowledgment.

quote: Unfortunately, not. We're with Mountain View. Okay. Mountain View. Okay. No problem. Which is good and bad. They're they're a little bit harder to deal with on solar, but, you know, they did I like the company.
stewart_read: Customer flags that his utility is harder to deal with on solar — a concrete net-metering-relevant detail for an expansion project. Rep responds only with 'No problem' and moves straight to the bill question without asking what specifically makes Mountain View difficult.
alternative_hypothesis: Rep may be scoping this correctly as closer-tier technical content (interconnection/net-metering specifics) rather than something the setter should dig into.
coaching_implication: Even under setter_scope_discipline, a 10-second follow-up ('what's been the tricky part with them?') would give the closer real competitive/utility intel instead of a dropped thread — flag as a missed 15-second probe, not a scope violation.

quote: Yeah. Yeah. I can send you a spreadsheet. I mean, I track it in the spreadsheet.
stewart_read: Customer reveals he personally tracks detailed production/usage data in a spreadsheet — a highly engaged, data-literate lead. Rep takes the offer at face value and pivots straight to sending a generic text rather than asking what the spreadsheet shows or using it to build anticipation for the appointment.
alternative_hypothesis: Rep efficiently accepted the fastest data-collection path available, which is the correct procedural move under bill_collection given this is an orphaned/organic-style lead.
coaching_implication: Efficient bill capture is fine; the miss is not asking one follow-up question ('what's that usually looking like month to month?') that would have built curiosity ahead of the specialist visit.

quote: So, yeah, if you can send that there And while you're doing that, let me pull up our schedule here and see what it's looking like.
stewart_read: Rep multitasks bill-collection wait time with schedule lookup, an efficient use of dead air rather than leaving the call silent.
coaching_implication: This is a positive efficiency habit worth noting to the rep as something to keep doing, not a gap.

quote: Could you do, like, 04:00? And would this be at the house, or would this be, somewhere or, you know, virtual?
stewart_read: The schema's button_up template (no_driving_at_computer, is_that_fair_handshake) is written for phone/virtual appointments; this call books an in-person home visit, and the rep never runs the 'is that fair?' handshake or a driving/computer instruction at all — there's no equivalent in-person confirmation substituted in its place.
alternative_hypothesis: The rep did confirm day, time, and location clearly ('So it will just be at the house... Thursday the thirtieth at four?'), which covers the functional booking need even without the verbal handshake phrase.
coaching_implication: Flag as a schema gap for Kenny: button_up currently has no in-person carve-out. Coach the rep to still close with an explicit 'does that work for both of you?' handshake regardless of channel — the mechanics, not just the logistics, are what predict show rate.

quote: Yes. You said it? Okay. Perfect. Well, yeah, just so you know, so I I always block off an hour for the customers for their appointment.
stewart_read: Rep does execute the one-hour block promise from button_up, a schema-compliant element even though the overall button-up is thin.
coaching_implication: Positive habit to reinforce — the rep knows this piece of the script even if she skips the handshake and driving/computer line.

quote: And then I will just send you a text with your appointment details as well just so you can add it to your calendar. Does that sound good?
stewart_read: Rep commits to the text-followup promise required by button_up and closes with a soft confirmation question, though it's a general 'does that sound good' rather than the schema's 'is that fair?' handshake.
coaching_implication: Acceptable substitute phrasing under strategy_recognition — the intent of the handshake is present even if the exact words differ.
